**Finding submitted — deviation (AUDIT), fallback-level cure.**

What I found across the document:

- **§ 7.4 Records; Inspection (p0481–p0483)** — largely acceptable: once each Calendar Year, one inspection per calendar quarter, independent nationally recognised accounting firm reasonably acceptable to Ono, confidentiality agreement required, Array bears cost. Two gaps: notice is only "reasonable prior written notice," and the underpayment cost-shift threshold is blank ("[ \* ]"), so the 10% trigger is not secured.
- **§ 4.9 Inspection Right (p0359–p0360)** — the material failure: Array or its representative may enter Ono's and its Affiliates' facilities and examine internal procedures and records to verify compliance "with this Agreement," on merely "reasonable advance notice" and with **no frequency limit**. That is unlimited-audit territory, and it survives termination (p0674).
- **§ 4.6(d)(ii) Audited Sites (p0340–p0343)** — Regulatory Authority inspections, not a Vendor audit right; not flagged.
- **§ 9 (p0503)** — inspection rights secured *for* Ono; benefits us, not flagged.

Cure (3 surgical replacements, validated ok:true): once-per-year cap plus 15 days' prior written notice in § 4.9; 15 days' prior written notice in § 7.4; cost-shift threshold fixed at ten percent (10%). I deliberately stopped at fallback rather than stripping § 4.9's on-site access, since deleting the facility-entry right would require collateral rewrites of the GxP compliance regime in Article IV — noted in the rationale.
